title: FDA uses AI to choose where to concentrate food inspections; an imported-seafood pilot ran for years
summary: Commissioner Marty Makary told a Senate committee in May 2025 that FDA uses AI to target food inspections; a multi-year imported-seafood AI pilot is mentioned; no outcome figures in the source.
account: Civil Eats reported on 27 May 2025 that FDA Commissioner Marty Makary, appearing before a Senate committee the previous week, said the agency was using AI to identify where to concentrate food inspections and that AI can sometimes find patterns faster than people, adding that a human reviews the information. The article notes that FDA had been working for several years on a pilot focused on imported seafood and had announced an agency-wide generative AI rollout, with an FDA spokesperson saying all centers would run on a unified platform by 30 June; a 2 June update records the launch of FDA's generative tool Elsa, said to be used in part to identify high-priority inspection targets. Jaydee Hanson of the Center for Food Safety is quoted on the risks of using AI amid staff cuts. No inspection outcome, detection or recall attributable to the AI is given. FDA's own pilot page returned 404 in this session and the Internet Archive was offline, so no official report could be read.
purpose: Prioritise food inspection targets, including imported seafood, using pattern recognition over agency data.
system: FDA AI inspection-targeting tools (imported seafood pilot; Elsa generative AI)
developer: U.S. Food and Drug Administration (details not in the fetched source)
taxonomy_note: Statements of use only; the type names better-targeted inspections, not a documented outcome.

ratings.reason: No figure on inspections targeted, violations found or seafood shipments flagged appears in the source.
No contamination detection or recall is attributed to the AI.

ai_role.statement: Only the Commissioner's testimony and an FDA spokesperson's statements, as reported by Civil Eats, describe the AI's use; no evaluation, outcome or official report was obtainable (fda.gov pilot page 404; Internet Archive offline during the session).

headline: FDA uses AI to target food inspections

later.note: On 2 June 2025 FDA announced the agency-wide rollout of its generative AI tool Elsa, which it said was already being used to identify high-priority inspection targets.
later.quote: June 2, 2025 Update: Today, the FDA announced the rollout of Elsa, its own generative AI tool. According to the news release, the agency “is already using Elsa to accelerate clinical protocol reviews, shorten the time needed for scientific evaluations, and identify high-priority inspection targets.”
